item.title: 'Consistency is valuable in governance' – this ancient saying is worth heeding by the German side: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31 01:02:00
Photo:VCG While Germany focuses on issues like market access, supply chain security, and industrial competition, China likewise places great importance on a fair business environment and the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises. What both sides need is to establish more effective communication and coordination mechanisms to identify a new balance of interests in areas such as industrial upgrading, technological innovation, and economic and trade rules. President Xi Jinping held talks with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier at the Great Hall of the People on Friday afternoon. This marks the return to China - after an eight-year hiatus - of Steinmeier, an old friend of the Chinese people. The visit comes at a pivotal juncture, as the two nations approach the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations, and at a critical moment when China-EU economic and trade ties, following multiple rounds of consultations, are seeking a period of relative stability. The two heads of state engaged in an in-depth exchange of views on a range of major issues, including China-Germany relations, China-EU cooperation, and global governance, sending a clear signal in favor of openness over isolation, and cooperation over confrontation. During the talks, President Xi stressed that consistency is valuable in governance. This ancient saying, drawn from the Confucian classic Book of Documents , encapsulates the ancient wisdom of the sages: effective governance requires sustained stability, while frequent, capricious policy shifts are to be avoided. This offers highly relevant insights for today's China-Germany and China-Europe relations, and is worth heeding by the German side. China adopts a forward-looking view of its relations with Germany and the EU, and does not allow temporary frictions to derail the broader trajectory of cooperation. Germany and the European side should work with China in the same direction, and maintain a "consistent" resolve amid changes unseen in a century. This, too, is a test of political wisdom. President Steinmeier noted that he has visited China eight times over the past 25 years, witnessing its rapid development and observing a fresh, evolving landscape with each trip. China's rapid development is truly worth a visit from our German friends who can bring back their fresh impressions to Germany, which will help deepen an accurate understanding between the two nations and open up new possibilities for mutually beneficial cooperation. This year, several core production units at BASF's integrated site in Zhanjiang have come online. As the first stop on his visit, President Steinmeier toured the Volkswagen R&D center in Hefei, East China's Anhui, where he saw firsthand the "intelligent brain" for vehicles - a system developed jointly by Chinese and German teams - and test-drove a new-energy vehicle equipped with advanced autonomous driving technologies. These vivid, concrete outcomes underscore a significant evolution in China-Germany cooperation: a transition from a relationship based on the complementarity of markets and technologies toward one defined by joint innovation. This is not a one-sided dynamic of dependency, but rather the result of market-driven choices and mutually beneficial cooperation. In recent years, there has been a growing sense of "dependency anxiety" regarding China within Germany, alongside an increasing tendency to interpret economic and trade issues through a security lens. While Germany's desire to strengthen its economic resilience is understandable, this objective is not at odds with deepening cooperation with China. The stability of China's policy toward Germany does not imply an absence of diverging interests; rather, it underscores that such differences should be addressed within the context of a long-term strategic relationship. While Germany focuses on issues like market access, supply chain security, and industrial competition, China likewise places great importance on a fair business environment and the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises. What both sides need is to establish more effective communication and coordination mechanisms, through which both sides can identify a new balance of interests in areas such as industrial upgrading, technological innovation, and economic and trade rules. China's continuous opening-up further creates conditions for German companies to participate in this process. The positive signals emanating from the meeting between the Chinese and German leaders inject new momentum into China-Europe relations. While the relationship has weathered various storms, the challenges that have emerged during the course of cooperation are simply issues that arise in the process of development and progress. As the Chinese often say, problems encountered during development should be resolved through further development; similarly, the Germans frequently remark that "life is not a parking lot, but a driving lane." From trade consultations regarding electric vehicles to multiple rounds of dialogue on industrial policy, the twists and turns experienced by China and the EU in recent years have consistently led back to the negotiating table - where, through equal dialogue, solutions addressing the legitimate concerns of both sides have been found. This clearly demonstrates that China and Europe are fully capable of properly handling the contradictions and differences that arise in the course of their development, and of returning to the correct positioning of their partnership. As the "bellwether" of the EU, Germany is well-positioned - and has a responsibility - to play a more active role in fostering rational dialogue between China and the EU, and in upholding open cooperation. Next year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Germany. For over half a century, Germany has gained significant development opportunities from China's economic growth. As China's economic structure and industrial capabilities evolve, Germany needs to make corresponding adjustments - starting with an updated understanding of China. If Germany aspires to play a greater role in the Asia-Pacific and in international affairs, it should recognize the value of China and Germany working together toward the same direction. The more turbulent and complex the world becomes, the more steadfast and confident China and Germany should remain in their cooperation. By staying on the right course, solidifying the foundation of mutual trust, and broadening the scope of collaboration - while resisting the pull of unilateralism and ignoring short-term, distracting noise - the two nations can continue to inject more positive energy into their bilateral relationship, China-EU relations, and global governance as a whole.

item.title: Xi meets German, Swiss presidents; talks to steady ties, signal resolve to manage differences via dialogue: analysts
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31 00:24:00
Top News Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday held separate meetings with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin in Beijing. During the meetings, the Chinese leader emphasized the importance of bilateral relations to China-Europe ties. Steinmeier's state visit to China, which lasts from October 27 to 31, marks his first trip to China in nearly eight years. Parmelin's work visit lasts from October 30 to November 1. Analysts said against a backdrop of China-Europe trade tensions and rising protectionism, the leader's back-to-back meetings with two European counterparts reflect China's consistent pragmatic approach to Europe, signaling intent to manage disputes via dialogue and offset protectionism with openness, injecting stability into overall China-Europe ties. Back-to-back meetings In the meeting with Steinmeier, Xi said that China's policy toward Germany is consistent, stable and predictable, and China is happy to see Germany play a greater role in European and international affairs. He expressed the hope that Germany will view China's development and its cooperation with China with an open and positive attitude, uphold a rational, pragmatic and friendly policy toward China, and adhere to mutual respect and equal treatment, which is a valuable experience for the sustained and sound development of China-Germany relations. In the meeting with Parmelin, Xi said that Switzerland is an important partner of China in Europe, and Swiss cooperation with China has always been at the forefront among European countries. He added that free trade cooperation has become the brightest highlight of China-Switzerland relations, which fully demonstrates the political courage and responsibility of the two countries in adhering to open cooperation, and highlights the unique leading role of both sides in promoting the building of an open world economy. China is willing to work with Switzerland to uphold openness, strengthen cooperation, promote a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, and jointly inject confidence and more certainty into the economic and trade cooperation between China and European countries, as well as into global economic development, Xi said. According to the Chinese Foreign Ministry, Switzerland was the first continental European country to sign a free trade agreement with China. 2026 marks the 10th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Switzerland innovative strategic partnership. In August this year, Switzerland once again became the first European country to conclude negotiations with China on upgrading their free trade agreement. After their meeting, the two leaders witnessed the signing of a protocol on upgrading free trade agreement and multiple cooperation documents in areas such as scientific research, employment and the media. Reuters described the deal as "one of the most favourable trade deals" Beijing has granted a European country, "bucking a broader global shift towards protectionism", and contrasts with "barriers to trade put up not only by the US administration but also, increasingly, the EU." Jin Ling, director of the Department for Global Governance and International Organizations at the China Institute of International Studies, said the latest round of China's head-of-state diplomacy carries forward China's long-standing pragmatic approach toward Europe, helping enhance mutual trust, dispel misgivings, counter outside noise, steady China-Europe relations and unlock more room for cooperation. On the same day, the Chinese leader held talks with the leaders from two European countries to advance cooperation, which underscores the resilience of China-Europe relations, as both sides acknowledge the challenges and strive to manage differences and seek solutions, said Jiang Feng, senior researcher at Shanghai International Studies University and president of the Shanghai Regional Studies Association. Chinese experts also noted that leaders from Germany and Switzerland, meeting with Chinese leadership on the same day, are highly representative. As the EU's largest economy with close industrial ties to China, Germany serves as a ballast for China-EU cooperation and has played an important role in cushioning and balancing previous trade disputes between China and Europe, said Jin. On the other hand, Jiang noted that as a neutral non-EU member, Switzerland has greater autonomy and is less susceptible to ideological overreach and securitization of issues. "China-Switzerland ties offer a model for Europe, and Europe should see China's development and opening-up as an opportunity," said Jiang. Opportunity and challenges In meeting with Steinmeier, Xi said that China has always viewed the EU as a partner, and is committed to developing China-EU relations with sincerity and goodwill. History and reality have repeatedly shown that for China and the EU, cooperation outweighs competition and consensus outweighs differences, Xi said. He added that as long as both China and the EU stay committed to the positioning of their partnership and maintain the tone of equal-footed dialogue, differences and problems can be resolved and will not hinder further development of China-EU relations. In a separate meeting with Parmelin, Xi said Switzerland has long played an important and exemplary role in China-Europe economic and trade exchanges. It is hoped that Switzerland will leverage its unique influence, and play a positive role in promoting an upward balance and the steady growth of China-Europe trade. The Swiss and German leaders' China visit follows the visit made by Bernd Lange, chair of the European Parliament's Committee on International Trade. Chinese Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao told Lange in their meeting on Tuesday that China and the EU are key forces in upholding the multilateral trading system, stressing that China is not the source of the EU's problems but a partner in solving them. Earlier this month, Wang also met with the European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maros Sefcovic in Beijing, as the two sides jointly chaired the second meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism. The two sides agreed on a list of outcomes, including 16 specific points of consensus covering trade and investment balance, export controls, intellectual property rights and WTO reform. Over the past 12 months, leaders from a number of European countries including France, the UK, Germany, Serbia and Slovakia have all visited China. The Chinese Foreign Ministry also announced on Friday that Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker will pay an official visit to China from November 2 to 7. However, trade tensions persist despite the recent progress. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on October 16 that the EU would propose further restrictions on Chinese imports, arguing that the deal on hybrid vehicles would not fix the trade imbalance, Reuters reported. Furthermore, Bloomberg reported on Monday that Brussels was planning to use "safeguard measures" to cut imports of products from sectors including chemicals, furniture and machinery from China. In response, a spokesperson of the Ministry of Commerce said on Thursday that China will take all necessary measures to safeguard its interests and the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese enterprises if the EU insists on imposing discriminatory restrictions on Chinese products. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz was on a tour of Singapore, Japan and South Korea this week. During his visit to Singapore on Tuesday, Merz warned against full economic decoupling from China but called for reducing what he described as "unhealthy, one-sided dependencies" in supply chains, technology and raw materials, Reuters reported. According to Jin, China-EU relations are now in a phase of overall stability amid divergences, with dialogue and dispute management as the priority. "Amid multiple crises such as energy strains, inflation, stagnation and social discontent, Europe has recognized the value of the Chinese market. It keeps engagement with China as a baseline, but is also building policy tools to boost its bargaining power," said Jin. "That breeds uncertainty: negotiations need give-and-take, not concessions won by pressure." Jiang Feng said the EU should follow Switzerland's example and handle China-EU trade frictions professionally, rather than politicizing or securitizing normal economic ties. In particular, the EU needs to recognize that China-EU trade relations require a systematic, comprehensive framework, said Jiang, noting that the priority is an early restart of talks on the China-EU Comprehensive Agreement on Investment.

item.title: China urges US to immediately revoke FCC restrictions on Chinese testing labs, vows to firmly defend interests
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 22:45:00
The Ministry of Commerce of China File photo: VCG China strongly opposes the US Federal Communications Commission's (FCC) latest restrictions on testing laboratories and urges the US to immediately revoke the measures, a spokesperson for China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) said on Friday, vowing that China will take further necessary measures to safeguard its rights and interests, if the US insists on going its own way. The remarks came after the FCC voted to approve measures that will, starting December 1, 2028, prohibit the authorization of testing laboratories, telecommunications certification bodies and laboratory accreditation bodies located in China and other so-called "non-reciprocal economies." The measures will also prohibit FCC-related testing, certification and accreditation activities in these economies. Asked to comment on that, the MOFCOM spokesperson said that China had noted the relevant developments, adding that the FCC has repeatedly introduced restrictive measures targeting China despite China's repeated representations, in violation of the important consensus reached between the leaders of the two countries. These actions have seriously harmed the interests of China and other relevant trading partners, undermined the stability of China-US economic and trade relations, and disrupted global industrial and supply chains, the spokesperson said. China is strongly dissatisfied with and firmly opposed to these actions, the spokesperson said, noting that China has already taken countermeasures in response to previous restrictions. Highlighting the important role of Chinese testing laboratories in the global testing and certification system, the spokesperson said they provide cost-effective support for the production and trade of communications electronics and intelligent manufacturing products worldwide. The US has disregarded the objective laws governing global economic development and the international division of labor in industrial cooperation, interfering with market choices through administrative means and forcibly pushing for the return of testing activities to the US, according to the spokesperson. Such moves will increase testing costs for businesses, prolong product delivery and iteration cycles, and ultimately harm the interests of US businesses and consumers, the spokesperson said. China has previously proposed negotiations on a bilateral mutual recognition agreement on multiple occasions, but the US has adopted an extremely passive and negative attitude, the spokesperson noted. The spokesperson stressed that China's door to resolving disputes through consultations remains open, urging the US to heed the calls of the business community, respect market principles, work with China in the same direction and immediately revoke the relevant measures. "If the US insists on going its own way, China will take further necessary measures to firmly safeguard its legitimate rights and interests," the spokesperson said. Global Times

item.title: How China's desert energy bases fuel the world's largest renewable energy system
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 22:19:00
A view of the energy storage area at the China Three Gorges Corporation's Ulanqab green power station in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region Photo: Courtesy of China Three Gorges Corporation At midday, more than 25,000 mirrors turn with the sun on a stretch of the Gobi in Jinta county, Northwest China's Gansu Province. Their reflections converge on a receiver high above the ground, where molten salt flowing through pipes absorbs the concentrated heat. The heat can be stored in tanks and used later to produce steam that drives a turbine. Even after sunlight fades from the mirror field, the energy collected during the day can continue generating electricity. For Zhao Bin, who had spent nearly a decade working in the region, the harsh landscape held an opportunity. "It is precisely this harsh environment that gives rise to exceptional wind and solar energy resources," the head of the Jinta multi-energy complementary project told the Global Times. Across China's deserts, Gobi and other arid areas, collectively known in Chinese as "shagehuang," large wind and solar bases are putting those resources to work. Their development increasingly involves coordinating generation, storage, transmission and the industries that use the electricity. Chinese President Xi Jinping emphasized on October 16 that green development is an inherent requirement of high-quality development, calling for efforts to coordinate high-quality development with high-level environmental protection. He made the remarks during an inspection trip to the city of Ulanqab, North China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. China has built the world's largest renewable energy system. By the end of 2025, its combined installed wind and solar power capacity had reached 1.84 billion kilowatts. The country plans to add about 1 billion kilowatts of wind and solar capacity during the 2026-2030 period, or roughly 200 million kilowatts a year, the People's Daily reported. China has also set a target for non-fossil fuels to account for 25 percent of energy consumption by 2030 and more than 30 percent by 2035, while aiming to bring total wind and solar capacity to 3.6 billion kilowatts by 2035. From the mirror fields of Gansu to the solar farms of the Kubuqi Desert and computing centers in Ulanqab, the practical challenge is to turn abundant but variable wind and sunlight into reliable electricity, local livelihoods and new industries. Power on the grassland In Ulanqab, a small change on a monitoring screen once brought that challenge into view for wind-power worker Xing Yichen. When Xing arrived at the green power station project of the China Three Gorges Corporation in Ulanqab in 2021, something unfamiliar caught his eye on an otherwise familiar monitoring screen: battery icons. He later learned that the new symbols represented equipment that would give the station another way to manage its electricity. Wind and solar generation rise and fall with the weather, often producing electricity at times that do not match demand. The batteries allow the station to store some of that electricity and release it later, helping bridge the gap between when power is generated and when it is needed, according to the Three Gorges Corp. Located on the grasslands of Siziwang Banner, the project combines 2 gigawatts of wind and solar generation with a 550-megawatt battery system that can discharge at full power for two hours. A coordinated control system assigns output among the turbines, solar installations and batteries in response to grid instructions, allowing them to work together to balance electricity supply and demand, according to the company. The company described how this works at its Jihong No. 1 station during the summer electricity-demand peak. When solar output surges around midday, batteries make short charging and discharging adjustments to capture electricity that would otherwise be curtailed. They can then release stored power quickly during the afternoon demand peak. Horses graze near wind turbines on the grassland in Ulanqab, North China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. Photo: VCG Winter brings a different operating pattern. Periods of strong renewable output can last longer, allowing the station to absorb larger quantities of surplus wind and solar electricity. Stored energy is then released when heating demand rises and the grid has room to receive it. These decisions also respond to the electricity market. Under the station's own dispatch arrangements, operators consider forecasts of renewable output and spot-market prices when deciding when to charge and discharge. Under direct grid dispatch, the batteries follow instructions intended to balance supply and demand. By the end of September, the project had generated about 3.22 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity during 2026, according to the company. Yet storage has not eliminated curtailment. The project recorded a 25.91 percent curtailment loss rate in the first nine months of 2026. Working with the land For residents living beside the projects, the changes can be seen close to the ground. In Guanjing village in Dalad Banner, Ordos, Inner Mongolia, villager Feng Hui pointed toward a solar project as he described its benefits to Xinhua in September 2025. Alongside ecological improvements, he cited compensation villagers received for the use of their land. At a Kubuqi solar project, farmers and herders have also been raising chickens and growing crops beneath the panels with guidance from desertification-control specialists. The activity adds another use to land already producing electricity. Making that combination work requires attention to the conditions around each panel. Zhao Jinquan, a construction manager at the Mengxi Kubuqi photovoltaic desertification-control project, explained that the panels provide shade and shelter from wind, reducing evaporation and improving growing conditions. Water used to wash the panels can also irrigate vegetation at the project, according to the report. The work extends beyond planting directly underneath the arrays. In an interview with the Global Times, Jin Jian, who headed a Chinese new energy company's office in the Middle East and Central Asia, described measures at a Kubuqi project that included windbreak belts, upright barriers made from sand willow branches, and drought-tolerant shrubs and grasses beneath the panels. Staff members inspect a solar power station in Ordos, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, on August 13, 2025. Photo: VCG Water availability remains a condition for such restoration. In an October account of its ecological work, the Ordos ecology and environment bureau said the city treats water resource carrying capacity as a prerequisite for ecological construction and chooses trees or grasses according to local conditions. In July, a new large-scale energy base entered the construction phase in the Kubuqi Desert. The project will bring together wind and solar power, energy storage and supporting thermal generation, with electricity to be transmitted to Shanghai through a planned ultra-high-voltage line. Hao Wenyi, general manager of Huaneng Kubuqi Power Generation Co, gave the People's Daily a sense of its dimensions: Driving from the southern to the northern end of the existing solar arrays took half an hour, although they represented only about one-eighth of the total planned capacity. The base has a planned installed capacity of 15.14 gigawatts and is expected to be completed in 2030. Following the electricity Alongside sending electricity to distant users, renewable-rich regions are developing industries that can use more of it nearby. In Ulanqab, that connection reaches into autonomous driving and scientific research. Xpeng's Fuyao autonomous-driving computing center and Fudan University's Qiewen No. 1 scientific computing cluster are both deployed at Alibaba Cloud's Ulanqab computing center, the city's big data bureau told the Global Times. The workloads give a concrete purpose to the servers being installed in the city: training driving systems and supporting research. Ulanqab's appeal combines renewable resources with a cool climate and its location near major markets. Local authorities are now working on how electricity infrastructure can support the computing industry's continued growth. At the Zhongjin Data low-carbon computing base, the first batch of an integrated generation, grid, demand and storage project was connected in July 2025. The project pairs computing demand with 200 megawatts of wind power, 100 megawatts of solar power and battery storage designed for four hours of operation. Once fully operational, the associated renewable generation is expected to replace 38.74 percent of the base's annual electricity consumption, according to the bureau. The figure describes the project's expected contribution at full capacity. The industrial opportunities extend into the equipment and services needed to build and operate these facilities. Chahar High Tech Development Zone has developed a wind power equipment chain covering turbines, blades, nacelle covers and supporting systems, the Global Times learned from the development zone. Around computing centers, businesses are producing electrical equipment and server cabinets, recovering and reusing servers, and providing maintenance, data services and training. The city's computing industry chain employs more than 1,600 people, according to the big data bureau. Local training is developing alongside those businesses. Ulanqab Vocational College and Huawei have jointly established an industry college that trains about 500 people annually in areas including computing resource scheduling and AI applications. As the renewable industry matures, another type of work is emerging around equipment reaching the end of its first service life. In August, Xinyuan Jiuquan, a subsidiary within China Resources Recycling Group's new energy business, began a project to remanufacture 25 retired wind turbines that had served for more than 15 years. Ageing equipment, declining generating efficiency and rising maintenance costs had brought the machines to retirement. Technicians inspect and assess their components, repair damage and restore transmission systems. A remanufactured prototype has been completed, with potential applications including distributed wind generation, small captive power stations and auxiliary industrial power supply. The project adds equipment recovery and reuse to the industrial activity surrounding renewable development. Back in Jinta, the technology used to operate the mirror field is also changing. In a June media report, a visitor from Kazakhstan asked Zhao whether the station used artificial intelligence. Zhao explained that AI tools were being introduced for abnormal-data alerts, assistance with electricity market decisions and on-site safety management. Staff could check monitoring data for the station through a mobile phone app - another tool for managing the electricity collected by the mirrors outside.

item.title: Guiding principles from CPC plenum in focus
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 21:42:00
The Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) holds a press conference on the guiding principles from the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee on Oct. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Xiaoyu) A resolution adopted at a plenary session of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee makes clear the CPC's resolve to stay firmly on a distinctive Chinese path to combating corruption, an official said at a press conference held by the CPC Central Committee on the guiding principles from the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee on Friday. At the press conference, Tang Fangyu, head of the Policy Research Office of the CPC Central Committee, hailed the resolution as the most important outcome of the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee. An editorial carried by People's Daily on Friday also described the resolution as a programmatic text for steadily pushing forward the great new project of strengthening the Party in the new era. The plenum, which concluded on Thursday in Beijing, adopted the Resolution of the Central Committee of the CPC on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance. The resolution underscored that the CPC has outlined four areas of focus for steadfastly following a distinctive Chinese path to combating corruption in the resolution, said Zhang Fuhai, deputy secretary of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection of the CPC and deputy head of the National Commission of Supervision. The four areas are maintaining a tough stance against corruption, strengthening checks on and oversight over the exercise of power, fortifying the cultural-ethical foundations for championing integrity and disdaining corruption, and enhancing coordinated efforts to prevent corruption by rooting out audacity, opportunity, and desire, according to Zhang. Since the 18th National Congress of the CPC in 2012, discipline inspection and supervisory organs across the country have filed 8.105 million cases and punished 7.922 million people, including 963 officials registered at and supervised by the CPC Central Committee, Zhang noted. Also speaking at the press conference, Hu Heping, deputy head of the Publicity Department of theCPC Central Committee, said that strengthening the Party spirit represents a fundamental task of efforts to ensure full and rigorous Party self-governance. The People's Daily's editorial said that the plenary session's focus on sustaining full and rigorous Party self-governance fully manifests the CPC's sharp awareness and unwavering resolve to strengthen self-improvement. At the press conference, Huang Jianfa, deputy head of the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee, said that the CPC has stressed the need to promote Party building in emerging sectors in a resolution adopted at the plenary session. Huang said the CPC will step up efforts to expand and deepen the coverage of Party organizations and Party work in new types of economic and social organizations, as well as among groups in new forms of employment, so as to strengthen the Party's appeal, cohesiveness and influence in emerging fields. New types of economic organizations encompass non-public-sector enterprises and businesses operating in emerging areas. New types of social organizations cover a broad range of entities, including industry associations, chambers of commerce, social service agencies and community-based organizations. New forms of employment have emerged alongside the growth of the internet and digital economy. They include workers such as food delivery couriers, ride-hailing drivers and online marketers, many of whom rely on digital platforms for their work. China currently has about 84 million people engaged in new forms of employment, who play an important role in meeting people's daily needs, supporting livelihoods and keeping economic activity running smoothly. The People's Daily's editorial also noted that the convening of the plenary session will surely galvanize and inspire the whole Party and people of all ethnic groups across the nation to strive for new glories on the new Long March. Global Times

item.title: China-US relations need stronger cultural ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 20:11:00
Students from the US show their handicrafts at a school in Shijiazhuang, North China's Hebei Province, on April 11, 2026. Photo: Xinhua The US Department of War's recent designation of Confucius Institutes in the US as a national security threat has added friction to China-US educational and cultural exchanges. At a recent press briefing, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun rejected the move as an act of stigmatization and reaffirmed the mutual benefits of educational cooperation between the two countries. This raises a broader question: How can China and the US deepen mutual understanding amid growing complexity in their relationship? Concerns about specific programs should be assessed on the basis of evidence and addressed through clear rules, while preserving opportunities for legitimate educational and cultural exchange. From a Chinese perspective, educational and cultural engagement is more than a supplement to bilateral diplomacy. It helps build mutual understanding, cultivate trust and sustain cooperation between societies with different historical experiences, cultural traditions and social systems. Such engagement cannot resolve every strategic disagreement, but it can help both sides understand the context in which the other's decisions are made. For decades, educational exchanges have connected generations of Chinese and Americans. Chinese students have studied at American universities, and American students and scholars have traveled to China to study the Chinese language, explore its history and understand its contemporary development. These experiences have shaped individual careers and created personal and professional networks that support bilateral relations. Firsthand experience provides insights that media reports or secondhand analysis alone cannot offer. In a September article, Rush Doshi of the Council on Foreign Relations and Rosie Levine of the US-China Education Trust warned that the US was losing its ability to train future China specialists. Their warning highlights a practical reason to sustain exchanges: Informed policymaking depends on people who understand the other country's society, institutions and perspectives. That expertise remains essential even when the two governments disagree on major issues. The September summit between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump in Washington created a window of opportunity to strengthen cooperation in this area. President Xi called for translating the new vision of a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability into action, striving for a relationship where "cooperation is the mainstay, competition is kept within proper limits, differences are managed and peace can be expected, and chart the right path for the two major countries to get along." The two leaders agreed to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. This common understanding provides important political guidance for the future development of the bilateral relationship. A cultural event during the visit illustrated how such engagement can make a difference. Peng Liyuan, wife of President Xi, and Melania Trump, wife of US President Trump, visited the National Museum of Asian Art, and watched American teenagers sing Chinese songs together. Peng encouraged them to continue studying the Chinese language and culture and to become envoys of friendship between China and the US. Such occasions can spark curiosity and personal connections; their lasting value depends on continued learning and interaction. During the visit, President Xi said 100,000 young Americans will be invited to visit China for exchanges and study over the next five years. The initiative demonstrates China's willingness to open its door wider for a younger generation and give them the opportunity to experience the country firsthand. Its long-term contribution will depend on the quality of those experiences and the relationship participants maintain afterward. Summit diplomacy has created momentum, but lasting progress requires institutions to carry it forward. Both countries could give greater attention to long-term academic partnerships, reciprocal student and faculty exchanges, joint research in areas of shared interest, and cooperation among think tanks and cultural institutions. These efforts should expand opportunities for students and scholars from both countries to study, teach and conduct research in each other's countries. Equally important is continuity. Exchanges are most valuable when they foster sustained relationships rather than end with a single visit. Universities, think tanks and other participating institutions could provide follow-up opportunities through joint projects, language study and alumni networks. Political agreements can create openings for cooperation, while sustained people-to-people engagement helps provide a durable social foundation necessary to support that cooperation. The aim should be to make educational and cultural exchanges a stable part of bilateral relations, capable of continuing through periods of disagreement. China and the US will continue to have differences. Yet differences need not stop their peoples from learning about each other, nor should they overshadow the many areas where cooperation can produce shared benefits. Strengthening educational and cultural ties would be a practical investment in mutual understanding and in a more resilient and constructive relationship. The author is an associate research fellow at the Central Compilation and Translation Bureau. opinion@globaltimes.com.cn

item.title: China's GJ-21, world's first operational large armed reconnaissance stealth UAV on amphibious assault ship, boasts three core strengths: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 18:32:00
The airborne unmanned warfare formation attends a military parade in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 3, 2025. China on Wednesday held a grand gathering to commemorate the 80th anniversary of the victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War. (Xinhua/Deng Hua) China's GJ-21 reconnaissance and strike stealth drone recently completed its first successful takeoff and landing aboard the Sichuan, the country's first Type 076 amphibious assault ship, marking a breakthrough in the Chinese Navy's ability to operate fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime combat platforms, according to the Xinhua News Agency. The GJ-21 is the Chinese military's first carrier-borne stealth drone integrating reconnaissance and strike capabilities. Its successful takeoff and landing demonstrate the Chinese Navy's capability to launch and recover fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime combat platforms. The GJ‑21 is the world's first large stealth strike and reconnaissance drone capable of operating from amphibious assault ships. This test marks the world's first catapult launch of a large stealth strike and reconnaissance drone from an amphibious assault ship, Chinese military affairs expert Zhang Xuefeng, told the Global Times on Friday. Zhang outlined GJ‑21's key strengths. First, it boasts outstanding stealth performance. Adopting a flying‑wing configuration and an S‑shaped top‑mounted air intake, the aircraft eliminates strong radar reflection sources and delivers excellent all‑aspect stealth capability. Its stealth performance is even superior to that of in‑service stealth fighters. Suited for striking heavily defended targets, it can serve as a vanguard asset to carry out "door‑kicking" suppression missions, according to Zhang. Moreover, GJ‑21 has a substantial combat radius. The flying‑wing design boosts subsonic cruise efficiency. Though its airframe is far smaller than the J‑35 and J‑20, its combat radius is comparable, said Zhang. GJ‑21 is also low‑cost and reusable. Unlike hypersonic missiles, it can be recovered and redeployed multiple times. It can also deploy small, low‑cost glide guided bombs. Under high‑tempo operations, it offers greater fire‑delivery efficiency with better cost control. If GJ‑21 is deployed aboard the Type 076 amphibious assault ship, coordination between the Type 076 and aircraft carrier will markedly enhance the carrier strike group's anti‑surface and land‑attack capabilities. Furthermore, it can team up with manned fighters for high‑risk, complex missions such as suppression of enemy air defenses. Manned fighters can clear an aerial corridor while GJ‑21 pushes forward to neutralize hostile ground targets and air defense systems, according to Zhang. The Sichuan, bearing hull number 51, is the first Type 076 amphibious assault ship independently designed, developed and built by China. Launched and named on December 27, 2024, it incorporates a fully automated landing guidance system, a new integrated power system, and electromagnetic catapult and arresting technology. It can carry fixed-wing drones, helicopters and amphibious equipment, according to Xinhua. Since its first sea trial in November 2025, the Sichuan has steadily conducted sea trials as scheduled, successfully completing equipment and system checks and tests of overall operational stability, per Xinhua.

item.title: Chinese tech firm gives employees gold keyboard keycaps for fifth straight year
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 14:05:00
A tech company in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, gave 20 gold keyboard keycaps to outstanding employees as gifts for Programmers' Day in China on October 24. Photos: Jimu News A tech company in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, gave 20 gold keyboard keycaps to outstanding employees as gifts for Programmers' Day in China on October 24. One of the keycaps, a gold space bar weighing about 35 grams, is worth more than 40,000 yuan ($6,000), Jimu News reported. The company, Insta360, an intelligent imaging technology firm, has presented gold keycaps to outstanding employees for five consecutive years, giving away a total of 75, according to the media report. Nearly 60 percent of its workforce is engaged in research and development (R&D), with R&D personnel playing a key role in driving product innovation. Each year, the largest gold space bar is awarded to the programmer who has made the greatest contribution to the company. This year, the company also introduced gold "F5" keys, symbolizing iterative improvement and innovation. Each F5 key is worth nearly 10,000 yuan, while all the keycaps are made of approximately 99.9 percent pure gold. With gold prices fluctuating, the gold keycaps have unexpectedly become a kind of "investment product" in employees' eyes, although many choose to keep them as souvenirs. In a post on his Sina Weibo account recently, Insta360 CEO Liu Jingkang said that a young colleague had suggested giving this year's gold keycaps to artificial intelligence (AI) instead of employees, but he disagreed. While AI has made it possible to generate code in ever-greater quantities, the value that exceptional people can create has actually become even greater, Liu said. As more code is generated by AI, the company still chooses to reward human creativity with real gold, he added. Global Times

item.title: Merz's flattery of Takaichi was politically frivolous
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 11:12:00
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi (R) and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz hold a joint press conference after their talks at the prime minister's office in Tokyo on October 28, 2026. Photo: VCG During his visit to Japan, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated that despite the geographical distance between the two countries, calling each other neighbors would not be an overstatement. He also described Germany and Japan as "Premium Partners," emphasizing that the two sides share similar interests and values. While expressing a sense of closeness is not unusual in diplomatic settings, characterizing two countries separated by 9,000 kilometers as "neighbors" - and using "shared values" as a pretext to advance a series of security and economic arrangements with clear, targeted objectives - goes well beyond mere rhetoric. By framing Germany and Japan as "neighbors," Merz is not truly referring to geography, but rather to political alignment. As developed economies, Germany and Japan share common interests in upholding multilateral trade and addressing climate change. However, these interests can be addressed through established bilateral and multilateral channels, without drawing lines based on "shared values." It is worth noting that Germany's postwar reflection on its own history has left a deep impression on nations across Asia. In contrast, since the current Japanese administration took office, there have been clear signs of a distorted view of history and moves toward "remilitarization," prompting neighboring countries to remain vigilant. By emphasizing "shared values" with Japan at this particular moment, how does Merz expect Asian countries to view Germany? In fact, Merz is doing more than just signaling closer ties with Japan; he has explicitly called for stronger military cooperation between the two countries. Germany has also expressed interest in joining the Global Combat Air Program - a joint initiative involving Japan, the UK, and Italy. The fact that two nations defeated in World War II are so eagerly moving to the forefront of military cooperation, while selectively emphasizing "shared values" and deliberately sidestepping the postwar international order's constraints on military activities, is in itself enough to warrant vigilance from the international community. On the Taiwan question, Merz also remarked that Germany will decide how to implement the one-China policy, an attempt to create a "gray area" on a matter of principle. Such attempts to test the boundaries are in no way constructive for China-Germany relations. Merz's flattery toward Takaichi goes beyond mere "cozying up" - it is a clear display of political frivolity. China has never opposed other nations developing normal relations; however, any cooperation implicitly directed against China deviates from the proper course of state-to-state relations. The German business community had generally hoped that Merz's trip to Asia would help secure orders and improve supply-chain links. Yet Merz has clearly failed to demonstrate the rationality expected of a mature political figure during this visit. The Chinese foreign ministry has previously expressed the hope that Germany and the EU will remain objective and rational, work with China in the same direction, and become reliable and predictable partners for each other. Merz would do well to heed this advice. One might attempt to "claim" a neighbor from 9,000 kilometers away, but genuine partnership requires sincerity and mutual respect.

item.title: From anxiety to calm: Chinese support transforms maternal, child healthcare in western Pakistan
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 08:49:00
This file photo shows medical supplies donated by China at a hospital in Quetta, Pakistan. (Xinhua) For 28-year-old Gul Bano, the birth of her fourth child brought something she had not experienced during her previous three deliveries -- a sense of calm. Two months ago, Bano arrived at a basic health unit in the provincial capital city of Balochistan to give birth. Unlike her earlier experiences, she found herself surrounded by modern medical equipment, trained health workers, and a clean, well-equipped delivery room. "This time, I was not afraid," Bano said, recalling the day her baby was born. "Everything was available here, and the delivery was much easier than it was a few years ago." Among the equipment that assisted her was a vein detector, which makes it easier to locate veins, particularly when an intravenous line or blood sample is needed, as well as a vacuum extractor, making it easier for her to deliver. For Bano, however, the difference was not only about medical equipment. She said the care she received made her feel respected and comfortable. "My husband works as a daily-wage laborer and earns less than 5 U.S. dollars a day, hindering us as a family from affording quality healthcare. Here, everything was provided to me free of charge, even the delivery gown. The bed was clean, and the equipment was ready," she said. "I did not have to worry about anything." Her experience reflects the changes taking place in maternal and child healthcare facilities across Balochistan. Supported by the government of China, these facilities are offering safer and more dignified childbirth services for mothers. China has been helping the government of Balochistan in upgrading maternal and child healthcare facilities, including the improvement of 100 medical facilities across the province. The cooperation aims to strengthen medical infrastructure, provide modern equipment, and improve services for mothers and newborns, particularly in areas where access to quality healthcare has traditionally been difficult. For women like Bano, these improvements are not simply about new machines or renovated rooms, but can mean the difference between approaching childbirth with anxiety and facing it with confidence. "I am very happy with the treatment I received," she said. "I thank China for helping us. My fourth child arrived not only as a new member of the family, but also as a reminder of how better healthcare can change a mother's experience at one of the most important moments of her life." Balochistan has the highest maternal and neonatal mortality rates in Pakistan, largely because 70 percent of the population lives in remote, scattered and hard-to-reach areas, Sana Furqan, a medical practitioner at the Basic Health Unit in the Hudda locality of Quetta, told Xinhua. "For decades, access has been the biggest barrier. This China-supported project is the first large-scale targeted intervention focused entirely on mothers and children at the primary healthcare level, bringing life-saving care to the doorstep of women in remote districts," she said. Talking about the newly equipped healthcare facilities and renovation, Furqan said the Chinese government has supplied equipment like ultrasound machines, delivery beds, baby warmers, incubators, and essential laboratory equipment. "This upgrade is going to bring proximity, preparedness, timeliness and continuity, which is critical to prevent deaths from postpartum hemorrhage, sepsis and birth asphyxia," she said, adding that it will also provide solar solutions, ambulances, as well as training for female staff. "The project would have transformative impacts on the basic healthcare system of Balochistan. In the medium term, we expect a measurable reduction in maternal mortality ratio and neonatal mortality rate, and a sharp decline in preventable complications," she added. Furqan believes the assistance is not seen as charity, but as brotherhood. "The people of Balochistan, especially its mothers, will never forget that when they needed help the most, China stood with them." In a conversation with Xinhua, Provincial Health Minister Bakht Muhammad Kakar said that Pakistan-China cooperation in the health sector is opening a new chapter in people-centered development, turning the friendship between the two countries into tangible benefits for communities. China has one of the most advanced, efficient, and equitable healthcare systems in the world, Kakar said, underlining that despite its own vast population, the country has achieved universal maternal and child health coverage, which is an inspiration for Pakistan. "We want to learn from China's experience in maternal health monitoring, village doctor system, and digital health records," the health minister said.
